rules.legal_concept: All persons entitled to public records
rules.atomic_rule: Any person (as defined) has a right, upon a sufficient written request to a public body's FOIA coordinator, to inspect, copy, or receive copies of a nonexempt public record.
rules.trigger: None stated (unconditional right, subject to exemptions and the incarcerated-person exclusion).
rules.source_language: It is the public policy of this state that all persons, except those persons incarcerated in state or local correctional facilities, are entitled to full and complete information regarding the affairs of government and the official acts of those who represent them as public officials and public employees, consistent with this act.
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared eligibility key. 'All persons' carries no requester-class limitation except the incarcerated carve-out captured separately (MI-0002).

rules.legal_concept: Incarcerated persons excluded from 'person'
rules.atomic_rule: An individual serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state, county, or federal correctional facility is not a 'person' entitled to make a request under the act.
rules.trigger: Requester is serving a sentence of imprisonment in a correctional facility.
rules.source_language: "Person" means an individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, firm, organization, association, governmental entity, or other legal entity. Person does not include an individual serving a sentence of imprisonment in a state or county correctional facility in this state or any other state, or in a federal correctional facility.
rules.notes: A requester-class gate that the software must branch on to reject ineligible requesters. Structural fork.

rules.legal_concept: No residency or citizenship qualification
rules.atomic_rule: Eligibility to request records extends to all persons with no residency or citizenship qualification.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: It is the public policy of this state that all persons, except those persons incarcerated in state or local correctional facilities, are entitled to full and complete information regarding the affairs of government
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared key, not a negative. Neither § 15.231(2) nor the 'person' definition in § 15.232(g) contains any residency or citizenship qualifier.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A requester need not state a purpose to obtain records; the required request contents are limited to a sufficient description plus name, address, and contact information.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: upon providing a public body's FOIA coordinator with a written request that describes a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find the public record, a person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive copies of the requested public record of the public body.
rules.notes: Universal-access symmetry: emitted as a rule with the shared key. The right attaches to a sufficient description; the act nowhere conditions access on a stated purpose. Verbatim clause enumerates the trigger; purpose is absent.

rules.legal_concept: Request must be in writing
rules.atomic_rule: A person desiring to inspect or receive a copy of a public record must make a written request to the public body's FOIA coordinator.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to invoke enforceable FOIA rights.
rules.source_language: Except as provided in section 3, a person desiring to inspect or receive a copy of a public record shall make a written request for the public record to the FOIA coordinator of a public body.
rules.notes: Michigan does not confer FOIA rights on oral requests; the enforceable-response machinery attaches only to a written request. Compare states permitting oral requests.

rules.legal_concept: Request must sufficiently describe the record
rules.atomic_rule: The written request must describe a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find the public record.
rules.trigger: Written request submitted.
rules.source_language: upon providing a public body's FOIA coordinator with a written request that describes a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find the public record, a person has a right to inspect, copy, or receive copies of the requested public record
rules.notes: 'Sufficiently to enable...to find' is a soft standard the public body applies; no statutory clarification-and-toll clock exists for insufficient descriptions (see material negatives).

rules.legal_concept: Request must include requester identity and contact information
rules.atomic_rule: A request (from a non-indigent requester) must include the requesting person's complete name, address, and valid contact information (telephone number or email); a non-individual must give its individual agent's information.
rules.trigger: Written request submitted by a person other than a qualifying indigent individual.
rules.source_language: A request from a person, other than an individual who qualifies as indigent under section 4(2)(a), must include the requesting person's complete name, address, and contact information, and, if the request is made by a person other than an individual, the complete name, address, and contact information of the person's agent who is an individual. An address must be written in compliance with United States Postal Service addressing standards. Contact information must include a valid telephone number or electronic mail address.
rules.notes: Indigent individuals under § 15.234(2)(a) are excepted from the identification requirement.

rules.legal_concept: Written request includes electronic transmission
rules.atomic_rule: A written request may be transmitted by facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic means.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: "Written request" means a writing that asks for information, and includes a writing transmitted by facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic means.
rules.notes: Format-of-intake permission; the timing consequence of electronic transmission is captured in MI-0009.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed receipt of electronic requests
rules.atomic_rule: An electronically transmitted written request is not 'received' (starting the response clock) until 1 business day after transmission; if delivered to spam/junk-mail, not received until 1 day after the body first becomes aware, and the body must log both times.
rules.trigger: Written request made by fax, email, or other electronic transmission.
rules.clock_spec: receipt deemed 1 business day after electronic transmission (or 1 day after body first becomes aware, if in spam/junk)
rules.source_language: A written request made by facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic transmission is not received by a public body's FOIA coordinator until 1 business day after the electronic transmission is made. However, if a written request is sent by electronic mail and delivered to the public body's spam or junk-mail folder, the request is not received until 1 day after the public body first becomes aware of the written request. The public body shall note in its records both the time a written request is delivered to its spam or junk-mail folder and the time the public body first becomes aware of that request.
rules.notes: Defines the start event for the 5-business-day response clock (MI-0016); not a clock effect itself but a receipt-timing calculation the calendar pass must apply.

rules.legal_concept: FOIA coordinator designation (municipal)
rules.atomic_rule: A city, village, township, county, or state department (or a body under its control) must designate an individual as its FOIA coordinator, responsible for accepting and processing requests and approving denials.
rules.trigger: Public body is or is controlled by a city, village, township, county, or state department.
rules.source_language: A public body that is a city, village, township, county, or state department, or under the control of a city, village, township, county, or state department, shall designate an individual as the public body's FOIA coordinator. The FOIA coordinator shall be responsible for accepting and processing requests for the public body's public records under this act and shall be responsible for approving a denial under section 5(4) and (5).
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: custodian designation drives routing. Municipal-facing.

rules.legal_concept: Default FOIA coordinator
rules.atomic_rule: In a county without an executive form of government the county board chairperson is the FOIA coordinator; for all other public bodies the chief administrative officer is the designated FOIA coordinator.
rules.trigger: No individual separately designated / body type not covered by § 15.236(1).
rules.source_language: In a county not having an executive form of government, the chairperson of the county board of commissioners is designated the FOIA coordinator for that county. ... For all other public bodies, the chief administrative officer of the respective public body is designated the public body's FOIA coordinator.
rules.notes: Routing default; determines who must respond when no separate designation is made.

rules.legal_concept: FOIA coordinator may delegate
rules.atomic_rule: A FOIA coordinator may designate another individual to accept and process requests and to approve denials on the coordinator's behalf.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: An FOIA coordinator may designate another individual to act on his or her behalf in accepting and processing requests for the public body's public records, and in approving a denial under section 5(4) and (5).

rules.legal_concept: Employee must forward request to coordinator
rules.atomic_rule: An employee of a public body who receives a request for a public record must promptly forward that request to the FOIA coordinator.
rules.trigger: An employee (not the coordinator) receives a request.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "promptly" from employee receipt
rules.source_language: An employee of a public body who receives a request for a public record shall promptly forward that request to the freedom of information act coordinator.
rules.notes: 'Promptly' is an undefined soft standard; internal routing step, not a numeric deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Law enforcement records management system non-custody referral
rules.atomic_rule: A public body maintaining a law enforcement records management system is not the custodian of records stored for a subscribing body; upon a request for such a record it must, within 10 business days, give written notice identifying the subscribing body and directing the requester to submit the request there.
rules.trigger: Request received by the LE records-management-system host for a record stored on behalf of a subscribing public body.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of request (written referral notice)
rules.source_language: If the public body that maintains a law enforcement records management system receives a written request for a public record that is stored on behalf of a subscribing public body, the public body that maintains the law enforcement records management system shall, within 10 business days after receipt of the request, give written notice to the requesting person identifying the subscribing public body and stating that the requesting person shall submit the request to the subscribing public body.
rules.notes: Michigan-specific routing fork with its own clock. Structural branch.

rules.legal_concept: Retention of written requests
rules.atomic_rule: A FOIA coordinator must keep a copy of all written requests for public records on file for no less than 1 year.
rules.trigger: A written request is received.
rules.clock_spec: floor: 1 year retention from request
rules.source_language: A freedom of information act coordinator shall keep a copy of all written requests for public records on file for no less than 1 year.
rules.notes: Legally required request-tracking retention (minimum), so included per the checklist's 'only if legally required' gate.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response
rules.atomic_rule: Unless the requester agrees otherwise in writing, a public body must respond to a request within 5 business days after receiving it by granting, denying, partially granting/denying, or extending.
rules.trigger: Public body receives a written request.
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of request (receipt per MI-0009 for electronic)
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the person making the request, a public body shall, subject to subsection (10), respond to a request for a public record within 5 business days after the public body receives the request by doing 1 of the following: (a) Granting the request. (b) Issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request. (c) Granting the request in part and issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request in part. (d) Issuing a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the public body shall respond to the request.
rules.notes: The 5-day window is a substantive response deadline (not a bare acknowledgment). Requester may waive/extend by written agreement.

rules.legal_concept: Permitted response dispositions
rules.atomic_rule: A timely response must take one of four forms: grant; written denial; partial grant with written partial denial; or a single extension notice.
rules.trigger: Response due under MI-0016.
rules.source_language: a public body shall...respond to a request for a public record...by doing 1 of the following: (a) Granting the request. (b) Issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request. (c) Granting the request in part and issuing a written notice to the requesting person denying the request in part. (d) Issuing a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the public body shall respond to the request.
rules.notes: The branch set the engine must execute at the response state.

rules.legal_concept: Extension of response period
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may extend the response period by issuing a notice extending it for not more than 10 business days.
rules.trigger: Public body issues an extension notice within the initial 5-business-day window.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: +10 business-days beyond the initial 5-business-day window
rules.source_language: Issuing a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the public body shall respond to the request.

rules.legal_concept: Only one extension per request
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not issue more than one notice of extension for a particular request.
rules.trigger: An extension notice has already been issued for the request.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 1 extension per request
rules.source_language: A public body shall not issue more than 1 notice of extension for a particular request.

rules.legal_concept: Contents of extension notice
rules.atomic_rule: An extension notice must specify the reasons for the extension and the date by which the public body will grant, deny, or partially grant/deny the request.
rules.trigger: Public body issues an extension notice.
rules.source_language: If a public body issues a notice extending the period for a response to the request, the notice must specify the reasons for the extension and the date by which the public body will do 1 of the following: (a) Grant the request. (b) Issue a written notice to the requesting person denying the request. (c) Grant the request in part and issue a written notice to the requesting person denying the request in part.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may stipulate response delivery method
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may stipulate that the public body's response be delivered by email, facsimile, or first-class mail, unless the body lacks the technological capability for an emailed response.
rules.trigger: Requester stipulates a delivery method for the response.
rules.source_language: A person making a request under subsection (1) may stipulate that the public body's response under subsection (2) be electronically mailed, delivered by facsimile, or delivered by first-class mail. This subsection does not apply if the public body lacks the technological capability to provide an electronically mailed response.

rules.legal_concept: Failure to respond = final determination to deny
rules.atomic_rule: Failure to respond within the response period constitutes a public body's final determination to deny the request if the failure was willful and intentional, or if the request was flagged (FOIA language within first 250 words, or FOIA keywords/code reference on the envelope or subject line).
rules.trigger: No timely response, AND (willful/intentional) OR (request carried the flagging language/keywords).
rules.clock_spec: terminal on expiry of the 5-business-day (or extended 10-business-day) response period
rules.source_language: Failure to respond to a request under subsection (2) constitutes a public body's final determination to deny the request if either of the following applies: (a) The failure was willful and intentional. (b) The written request included language that conveyed a request for information within the first 250 words of the body of a letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or electronic mail attachment, or specifically included the words, characters, or abbreviations for "freedom of information", "information", "FOIA", "copy", or a recognizable misspelling of such, or appropriate legal code reference to this act, on the front of an envelope or in the subject line of an electronic mail, letter, or facsimile cover page.
rules.notes: Keeper-sliver: the constructive-denial trigger (silence = deemed denial). Damages remedy attached to it is captured/limited separately; only the terminal trigger is configured here.

rules.legal_concept: Written denial is final determination
rules.atomic_rule: A written notice denying a request in whole or in part is the public body's final determination to deny; it must contain the statutorily required contents.
rules.trigger: Public body denies a request in whole or in part.
rules.source_language: A written notice denying a request for a public record in whole or in part is a public body's final determination to deny the request or portion of that request. The written notice must contain:
rules.notes: Parent row for the denial-notice content requirements MI-0024 through MI-0028.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must explain exemption basis
rules.atomic_rule: If a record or portion is denied as exempt, the written denial must explain the basis under the act or other statute for that exemption determination.
rules.trigger: Denial based on an exemption.
rules.source_language: An explanation of the basis under this act or other statute for the determination that the public record, or portion of that public record, is exempt from disclosure, if that is the reason for denying all or a portion of the request.

rules.legal_concept: Certificate that record does not exist
rules.atomic_rule: If the denial is because the record does not exist, the written notice must contain a certificate that the record does not exist under the name given or another name reasonably known to the public body.
rules.trigger: Denial because the requested record does not exist.
rules.source_language: A certificate that the public record does not exist under the name given by the requester or by another name reasonably known to the public body, if that is the reason for denying the request or a portion of the request.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must describe separated/deleted material
rules.atomic_rule: If a separation or deletion is made, the written notice must describe the public record or information that was separated or deleted under section 14.
rules.trigger: Exempt material separated or deleted from a produced record.
rules.source_language: A description of a public record or information on a public record that is separated or deleted under section 14, if a separation or deletion is made.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must explain appeal rights
rules.atomic_rule: The written denial must fully explain the requester's right both to submit a written 'appeal' to the head of the public body and to seek judicial review of the denial under section 10.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: A full explanation of the requesting person's right to do either of the following: (i) Submit to the head of the public body a written appeal that specifically states the word "appeal" and identifies the reason or reasons for reversal of the disclosure denial. (ii) Seek judicial review of the denial under section 10.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must give notice of fees/damages right
rules.atomic_rule: The written denial must include notice of the right to receive attorneys' fees and damages if, after judicial review, the court finds noncompliance and orders disclosure.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a written denial.
rules.source_language: Notice of the right to receive attorneys' fees and damages as provided in section 10 if, after judicial review, the court determines that the public body has not complied with this section and orders disclosure of all or a portion of a public record.

rules.legal_concept: Denial must be signed by responsible individual
rules.atomic_rule: The individual designated as responsible for the denial must sign the written notice of denial.
rules.trigger: A written denial is issued.
rules.source_language: The individual designated in section 6 as responsible for the denial of the request shall sign the written notice of denial.

rules.legal_concept: Separation of exempt and nonexempt material
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains both exempt and nonexempt material, the public body must separate them and make the nonexempt material available for examination and copying.
rules.trigger: Requested record contains both exempt and nonexempt material.
rules.source_language: If a public record contains material which is not exempt under section 13, as well as material which is exempt from disclosure under section 13, the public body shall separate the exempt and nonexempt material and make the nonexempt material available for examination and copying.
rules.notes: Shared segregability key.

rules.legal_concept: Design records to facilitate separation
rules.atomic_rule: When designing a record the public body must, to the extent practicable, facilitate separation of exempt from nonexempt information, and must generally describe exempted material unless the description would defeat the exemption.
rules.trigger: Public body designs a public record; separation is readily apparent to a requester.
rules.source_language: When designing a public record, a public body shall, to the extent practicable, facilitate a separation of exempt from nonexempt information. If the separation is readily apparent to a person requesting to inspect or receive copies of the form, the public body shall generally describe the material exempted unless that description would reveal the contents of the exempt information and thus defeat the purpose of the exemption.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for re-redacting previously redacted record
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge for redaction labor if it knows or has reason to know it previously redacted the record and the redacted version is still in its possession.
rules.trigger: Public body previously redacted the same record and retains the redacted version.
rules.source_language: A public body shall not charge for labor directly associated with redaction under section 14 if it knows or has reason to know that it previously redacted the public record in question and the redacted version is still in the public body's possession.

rules.legal_concept: Fee limited to actual incremental cost
rules.atomic_rule: A permitted fee is limited to actual mailing costs and the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication, including labor and the cost of search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material, and the total must not exceed the sum of the six enumerated components.
rules.trigger: Public body charges or estimates a fee.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: sum of the 6 enumerated components (actual incremental cost)
rules.source_language: the fee must be limited to actual mailing costs, and to the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication including labor, the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14. Except as otherwise provided in this act, if the public body estimates or charges a fee in accordance with this act, the total fee must not exceed the sum of the following components:
rules.notes: Umbrella fee-cap; the six components are MI-0034/0036/0037/0038/0039/0040.

rules.legal_concept: Search labor rate — lowest-paid capable employee
rules.atomic_rule: Labor for searching, locating, and examining records may not be charged at more than the hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of doing so, regardless of who performs the labor.
rules.trigger: Public body charges search/location/examination labor.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee
rules.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of searching for, locating, and examining the public records in the particular instance regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor.
rules.notes: Shared labor-rate ceiling key.

rules.legal_concept: Labor charged in 15-minute increments, rounded down
rules.atomic_rule: Search/examination labor costs must be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
rules.trigger: Public body charges search/examination labor.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: 15-minute increments, partial increments rounded down
rules.source_language: Labor costs under this subdivision shall be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
rules.notes: Same increment rule also applies to redaction labor under (1)(b); duplication labor (1)(e) allows increments of the body's choosing rounded down.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction/separation labor rate ceiling
rules.atomic_rule: Labor to separate/delete exempt from nonexempt information may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid capable employee; if none is employed, contracted labor may be charged like employee labor but not exceeding 6 times the state minimum hourly wage.
rules.trigger: Public body charges separation/deletion (redaction) labor.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: lowest-paid capable employee wage; contracted labor <= 6x state minimum hourly wage
rules.source_language: For services performed by an employee of the public body, the public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of separating and deleting exempt information from nonexempt information in the particular instance... Total labor costs calculated under this subdivision for contracted labor costs must not exceed an amount equal to 6 times the state minimum hourly wage rate determined under section 4 of the improved workforce opportunity wage act, 2018 PA 337, MCL 408.934.
rules.notes: Contracted-labor ceiling references a moving external figure (state minimum wage).

rules.legal_concept: Nonpaper physical media at actual economical cost
rules.atomic_rule: For records provided on nonpaper physical media, the charge is limited to the actual and most reasonably economical cost of that media.
rules.trigger: Records provided on nonpaper physical media.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual most-economical cost of the nonpaper media
rules.source_language: For public records provided to the requestor on any form of nonpaper physical media, the actual and most reasonably economical cost of the nonpaper physical media.
rules.notes: Does not apply if the body lacks the technological capability for the stipulated media.

rules.legal_concept: Paper copy charge ceiling — 10 cents per sheet
rules.atomic_rule: The charge for paper copies must not exceed 10 cents per sheet for copies made on 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper, calculated as a total cost per sheet.
rules.trigger: Public body provides paper copies.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: $0.10 per sheet (8.5x11 or 8.5x14)
rules.source_language: The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper. A public body shall utilize the most economical means available for making copies of public records, including using double-sided printing, if cost saving and available.
rules.notes: Shared per-page copy-rate ceiling key. Excludes labor (which is separately capped).

rules.legal_concept: Duplication/publication labor rate ceiling
rules.atomic_rule: Labor directly associated with duplication or publication (paper or digital copies, transfers) may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid employee capable of the duplication.
rules.trigger: Public body charges duplication/publication labor.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee; increments of body's choosing, rounded down
rules.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of necessary duplication or publication in the particular instance, regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor. Labor costs under this subdivision may be estimated and charged in time increments of the public body's choosing; however, all partial time increments shall be rounded down.

rules.legal_concept: Actual mailing cost only
rules.atomic_rule: Mailing may be charged at actual cost in a reasonably economical manner; no charge for expedited shipping or insurance unless stipulated by the requester.
rules.trigger: Public body mails records.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of least-expensive economical mailing (plus delivery confirmation)
rules.source_language: The actual cost of mailing, if any, for sending the public records in a reasonably economical and justifiable manner. The public body shall not charge more for expedited shipping or insurance unless specifically stipulated by the requestor, but may otherwise charge for the least expensive form of postal delivery confirmation when mailing public records.

rules.legal_concept: Up to 50% fringe-benefit add-on to labor
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge to cover fringe benefits, not exceeding the actual cost of fringe benefits, if it notes the multiplier on the itemization.
rules.trigger: Public body charges labor and elects to recover fringe benefits.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: +50% of the applicable labor charge (capped at actual fringe cost)
rules.source_language: The public body may also add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge amount to cover or partially cover the cost of fringe benefits if it clearly notes the percentage multiplier used to account for benefits in the detailed itemization described in subsection (4). Subject to the 50% limitation, the public body shall not charge more than the actual cost of fringe benefits, and overtime wages shall not be used in calculating the cost of fringe benefits.
rules.notes: A higher multiplier is allowed only in the narrow website-then-paper scenario under § 15.234(5).

rules.legal_concept: Overtime excluded from labor unless stipulated
rules.atomic_rule: Overtime wages may not be included in labor-cost calculations unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requester and noted on the itemization.
rules.trigger: Labor performed on overtime.
rules.source_language: Overtime wages shall not be included in the calculation of labor costs unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requestor and clearly noted on the detailed itemization described in subsection (4).

rules.legal_concept: First $20 free for indigent / designated nonprofit
rules.atomic_rule: A record search and copies must be furnished without charge for the first $20 of the fee for each request by a qualifying indigent individual (with affidavit) or by a state-designated developmental-disabilities/mental-illness protection-and-advocacy nonprofit.
rules.trigger: Requester is a qualifying indigent individual or a qualifying designated nonprofit.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: first $20.00 of the fee waived per request
rules.source_language: A public record search shall be made and a copy of a public record shall be furnished without charge for the first $20.00 of the fee for each request by either of the following: (a) An individual who is entitled to information under this act and who submits an affidavit stating that the individual is indigent and receiving specific public assistance or, if not receiving public assistance, stating facts showing inability to pay the cost because of indigency.
rules.notes: Indigent ineligible if already received the discount twice that calendar year from the same body, or if request is in conjunction with paying outside parties. Nonprofit conditions in § 15.234(2)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Discretionary public-interest fee waiver/reduction
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may search for or furnish copies without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines a waiver/reduction is in the public interest because the disclosure primarily benefits the general public.
rules.trigger: Public body determines disclosure primarily benefits the general public.
rules.source_language: A search for a public record may be conducted or copies of public records may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge if the public body determines that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because searching for or furnishing copies of the public record can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public.
rules.notes: Discretionary; 'public interest / primarily benefiting the general public' is a soft standard.

rules.legal_concept: Search/redaction labor chargeable only if not charging would cause unreasonably high costs
rules.atomic_rule: A fee for search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material may not be charged unless failure to charge would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request, and the body specifically identifies the nature of those costs.
rules.trigger: Public body wishes to charge search/examination/review/separation labor.
rules.source_language: A fee as described in subsection (1) shall not be charged for the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14 unless failure to charge a fee would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request in the particular instance, and the public body specifically identifies the nature of these unreasonably high costs.
rules.notes: A gate the engine must evaluate before charging labor components; structural condition, not a value.

rules.legal_concept: No charge for records already on the body's website
rules.atomic_rule: Public records available to the general public on the body's website at the time of the request are exempt from separation/deletion labor charges under (1)(b).
rules.trigger: Requested records are available on the body's public website when the request is made.
rules.source_language: If the public body directly or indirectly administers or maintains an official internet presence, any public records available to the general public on that internet site at the time the request is made are exempt from any charges under subsection (1)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Notify requester of records available on website
rules.atomic_rule: If the coordinator knows or has reason to know requested information is on the body's website, the written response must so notify the requester and, to the degree practicable, include the specific webpage address.
rules.trigger: Coordinator knows/has reason to know requested info is on the website.
rules.source_language: If the FOIA coordinator knows or has reason to know that all or a portion of the requested information is available on its website, the public body shall notify the requestor in its written response that all or a portion of the requested information is available on its website. The written response, to the degree practicable in the specific instance, must include a specific webpage address where the requested information is available.
rules.notes: Shared website-redirect key. If requester later stipulates paper/other format, the body must still provide it (may exceed the 50% fringe cap up to actual cost).

rules.legal_concept: Standard itemized fee form
rules.atomic_rule: A public body's procedures must use a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee that clearly lists and explains the allowable charges for each of the six fee components used in estimating or charging.
rules.trigger: Public body estimates or charges a fee.
rules.source_language: A public body's procedures and guidelines must include the use of a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee amount in its responses to written requests under this act. The detailed itemization must clearly list and explain the allowable charges for each of the 6 fee components listed under subsection (1) that compose the total fee used for estimating or charging purposes.
rules.notes: DTMB provides a model form; a body may create its own compliant form.

rules.legal_concept: Procedures, guidelines, and written public summary
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must establish procedures and guidelines to implement the act and create a written public summary (how to submit requests, understand responses, deposits, fee calculations, and appeals), post them on any website, and provide free copies with responses and on request.
rules.trigger: Public body is subject to the act.
rules.source_language: A public body shall establish procedures and guidelines to implement this act and shall create a written public summary of the specific procedures and guidelines relevant to the general public regarding how to submit written requests to the public body and explaining how to understand a public body's written responses, deposit requirements, fee calculations, and avenues for challenge and appeal.
rules.notes: Procedures/guidelines are themselves non-exempt public records.

rules.legal_concept: No fees/deposits until procedures published
rules.atomic_rule: A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, created a written public summary, or made them publicly available free may not require deposits or charge fees until it is in compliance.
rules.trigger: Public body lacks published procedures/guidelines/summary.
rules.source_language: A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, has not created a written public summary, or has not made those items publicly available without charge as required in this subsection is not relieved of its duty to comply with any requirement of this act and shall not require deposits or charge fees otherwise permitted under this act until it is in compliance with this subsection.
rules.notes: Gate on the fee/deposit machinery.

rules.legal_concept: 5%-per-day labor-fee reduction for late response
rules.atomic_rule: If a public body does not respond timely and the lateness was willful/intentional or the request was flagged, it must reduce labor-cost charges by 5% for each day it exceeds the response deadline, up to a 50% maximum reduction.
rules.trigger: Untimely response AND (willful/intentional) OR (request carried FOIA flagging language/keywords).
rules.clock_spec: fixed: -5% of labor charge per late day, capped at -50%
rules.source_language: Reduce the charges for labor costs otherwise permitted under this section by 5% for each day the public body exceeds the time permitted under section 5(2) for a response to the request, with a maximum 50% reduction, if either of the following applies: (i) The late response was willful and intentional. (ii) The written request included language that conveyed a request for information within the first 250 words of the body of a letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or electronic mail attachment, or specifically included the words, characters, or abbreviations for "freedom of information", "information", "FOIA", "copy", or a recognizable misspelling of such, or appropriate legal code reference for this act, on the front of an envelope, or in the subject line of an electronic mail, letter, or facsimile cover page.
rules.notes: Fee-calculation remedy tied to lateness; reduces only the labor components.

rules.legal_concept: Fee section inapplicable to statutorily-priced records
rules.atomic_rule: The fee section does not apply to records prepared under a statute specifically authorizing their sale, or where another act/statute specifically sets the copy fee.
rules.trigger: Requested record has a statutorily-authorized sale price or a specifically-provided copy fee.
rules.source_language: This section does not apply to public records prepared under an act or statute specifically authorizing the sale of those public records to the public, or if the amount of the fee for providing a copy of the public record is otherwise specifically provided by an act or statute.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith deposit permitted above $50
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require a good-faith deposit before providing records if the entire estimated fee or charge exceeds $50, based on a good-faith total-fee calculation.
rules.trigger: Good-faith fee estimate exceeds $50.00.
rules.clock_spec: floor: deposit only allowed when estimate exceeds $50.00
rules.source_language: the public body may require a good-faith deposit from the person requesting information before providing the public records to the requestor if the entire fee estimate or charge authorized under this section exceeds $50.00, based on a good-faith calculation of the total fee described in subsection (4).

rules.legal_concept: Deposit capped at one-half of estimate
rules.atomic_rule: A good-faith deposit must not exceed one-half of the total estimated fee, and the deposit request must include a detailed fee itemization.
rules.trigger: Public body requires a good-faith deposit under § 15.234(8).
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 1/2 of the total estimated fee
rules.source_language: Subject to subsection (10), the deposit must not exceed 1/2 of the total estimated fee, and a public body's request for a deposit must include a detailed itemization as required under subsection (4).

rules.legal_concept: Best-efforts time-frame estimate with deposit
rules.atomic_rule: A deposit response must contain a good-faith best-efforts estimate of the time frame to provide the records; the estimate is nonbinding but must be made in good faith.
rules.trigger: Public body requires a deposit / responds under § 15.235(2)(d).
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: nonbinding best-efforts time-frame estimate
rules.source_language: The response must also contain a best efforts estimate by the public body regarding the time frame it will take the public body to comply with the law in providing the public records to the requestor. The time frame estimate is nonbinding upon the public body, but the public body shall provide the estimate in good faith and strive to be reasonably accurate
rules.notes: Nonbinding soft time-frame; not a production deadline.

rules.legal_concept: Up to 100% deposit for prior non-payers
rules.atomic_rule: For a subsequent request from an individual who did not pay in full for a prior fulfilled request, the body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before beginning the search, if six enumerated conditions are all met.
rules.trigger: Individual left a prior granted-and-fulfilled request unpaid and the six conditions in § 15.234(11)(a)-(f) are all satisfied.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 100% of estimated fee (only when all six conditions met, incl. 90 days since availability notice)
rules.source_language: after a public body has granted and fulfilled a written request from an individual under this act, if the public body has not been paid in full the total amount under subsection (1)...the public body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before it begins a full public record search for any subsequent written request from that individual if all of the following apply:
rules.notes: Conditions include: prior final fee <=105% of estimate; records still in possession; 90 days since availability notice; no proof of prior payment; detailed itemization. Structural branch with a parameter ceiling.

rules.legal_concept: Termination of 100% deposit authority
rules.atomic_rule: The body must stop requiring the increased (up to 100%) deposit if the individual shows proof of prior full payment, the body is later paid in full, or 365 days have passed since the unpaid request was made.
rules.trigger: Proof of payment shown, prior request paid in full, or 365 days elapsed since the unpaid request.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: 365 days from the unpaid written request extinguishes the increased-deposit authority
rules.source_language: A public body shall no longer require an increased estimated fee deposit from an individual as described under subsection (11) if any of the following apply: (a) The individual is able to show proof of prior payment in full to the public body. (b) The public body is subsequently paid in full for the applicable prior written request. (c) Three hundred sixty-five days have passed since the individual made the written request for which full payment was not remitted to the public body.

rules.legal_concept: A required deposit is a fee
rules.atomic_rule: A deposit required by a public body under the act is itself a 'fee.'
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: A deposit required by a public body under this act is a fee.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on: a deposit is appealable as a fee under § 15.240a.

rules.legal_concept: Request abandoned if deposit unpaid within 45 days
rules.atomic_rule: If a required deposit is not received within 45 days after the requester's receipt of the deposit notice, and no deposit-amount appeal was filed, the request is considered abandoned and the body need no longer fulfill it.
rules.trigger: Deposit not received within 45 days of receipt of the deposit notice and no § 15.240a appeal filed.
rules.clock_spec: terminal: 45 days from requester's receipt of the deposit notice
rules.source_language: If a deposit that is required under subsection (8) or (11) is not received by the public body within 45 days from receipt by the requesting person of the notice that a deposit is required, and if the requesting person has not filed an appeal of the deposit amount pursuant to section 10a, the request shall be considered abandoned by the requesting person and the public body is no longer required to fulfill the request.
rules.notes: Terminal state (abandonment). Keeper-sliver-style deemed disposition.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed receipt of deposit notice
rules.atomic_rule: A deposit notice is considered received 3 days after it is sent (regardless of transmission means), and it must state the deposit-due date, which is 48 days after the notice is sent.
rules.trigger: Public body sends a deposit-requirement notice.
rules.clock_spec: fixed: notice deemed received 3 days after sent; due date 48 days after sent
rules.source_language: Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) is considered received 3 days after it is sent, regardless of the means of transmission. Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) must include notice of the date by which the deposit must be received, which date is 48 days after the date the notice is sent.
rules.notes: Start-event calculation for the 45-day abandonment clock (MI-0059).

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable opportunity to inspect during business hours
rules.atomic_rule: A public body must furnish a reasonable opportunity for inspection and examination of its records, and reasonable facilities for making memoranda or abstracts, during the usual business hours.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks to inspect records.
rules.source_language: A public body shall furnish a requesting person a reasonable opportunity for inspection and examination of its public records, and shall furnish reasonable facilities for making memoranda or abstracts from its public records during the usual business hours.
rules.notes: 'Usual business hours' / 'reasonable' are soft standards the city fills in.

rules.legal_concept: Reasonable rules to protect records
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may make reasonable rules necessary to protect its records and prevent excessive and unreasonable interference with its functions, and must protect records from loss, alteration, or destruction.
rules.trigger: None stated.
rules.source_language: A public body may make reasonable rules necessary to protect its public records and to prevent excessive and unreasonable interference with the discharge of its functions. A public body shall protect public records from loss, unauthorized alteration, mutilation, or destruction.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a new record
rules.atomic_rule: The act does not require a public body to create a new public record, except as required in section 11 and to the extent needed to furnish copies or edited copies of an existing record.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating a record that does not exist.
rules.source_language: This act does not require a public body to create a new public record, except as required in section 11, and to the extent required by this act for the furnishing of copies, or edited copies pursuant to section 14(1), of an already existing public record.
rules.notes: Shared no-duty-to-create key.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to compile a summary or report
rules.atomic_rule: The act does not require a public body to make a compilation, summary, or report of information, except as required in section 11.
rules.trigger: Request would require compiling a summary/report.
rules.source_language: This act does not require a public body to make a compilation, summary, or report of information, except as required in section 11.

rules.legal_concept: Certified copies on written request
rules.atomic_rule: The custodian of a public record must, upon written request, furnish a requester a certified copy of the record.
rules.trigger: Written request for a certified copy.
rules.source_language: The custodian of a public record shall, upon written request, furnish a requesting person a certified copy of a public record.

rules.legal_concept: Subscription to future regular issuances
rules.atomic_rule: A person may subscribe to future issuances of public records created/issued/disseminated on a regular basis; a subscription is valid for up to 6 months at the subscriber's request and is renewable.
rules.trigger: Requester subscribes to a regularly-issued public record series.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: subscription valid up to 6 months, renewable
rules.source_language: A person has a right to subscribe to future issuances of public records that are created, issued, or disseminated on a regular basis. A subscription is valid for up to 6 months, at the request of the subscriber, and is renewable.

rules.legal_concept: Requester may stipulate electronic/nonpaper format
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may stipulate that records be provided on nonpaper physical media, electronically mailed, or otherwise electronically provided in lieu of paper copies, unless the body lacks the technological capability for the particular media.
rules.trigger: Requester stipulates a nonpaper/electronic delivery format.
rules.source_language: The requestor may stipulate that the public records be provided on nonpaper physical media, electronically mailed, or otherwise electronically provided to him or her in lieu of paper copies. This subdivision does not apply if a public body lacks the technological capability necessary to provide records on the particular nonpaper physical media stipulated in the particular instance.
rules.notes: Shared format-election key.

rules.legal_concept: Records may be provided without a written request
rules.atomic_rule: A public body may provide requested information available in public records without receipt of a written request; and for a verbal request believed to be on the website, the employee should, where practicable, inform the requester of the pertinent website address.
rules.trigger: Informal or verbal request received.
rules.source_language: A public body may provide requested information available in public records without receipt of a written request. If a verbal request for information is for information that a public body believes is available on the public body's website, the public employee shall, where practicable and to the best of the public employee's knowledge, inform the requestor about the public body's pertinent website address.
rules.notes: Informal path; does not trigger the enforceable § 15.235 response machinery, which requires a written request.

rules.legal_concept: Written appeal to head of public body
rules.atomic_rule: After a final determination to deny all or part of a request, the requester may submit to the head of the public body a written appeal that specifically states the word 'appeal' and identifies the reasons for reversal.
rules.trigger: Public body issues a final determination to deny in whole or part.
rules.source_language: If a public body makes a final determination to deny all or a portion of a request, the requesting person may do 1 of the following at his or her option: (a) Submit to the head of the public body a written appeal that specifically states the word "appeal" and identifies the reason or reasons for reversal of the denial.
rules.notes: Administrative-appeal stage (namespaced). Optional; requester may instead go straight to circuit court.

rules.legal_concept: Head must decide appeal within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: Within 10 business days after receiving a written appeal, the head of the public body must reverse, uphold, partially reverse/uphold, or (under unusual circumstances) extend.
rules.trigger: Head of public body receives a written appeal.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of written appeal
rules.source_language: Within 10 business days after receiving a written appeal pursuant to subsection (1)(a), the head of a public body shall do 1 of the following: (a) Reverse the disclosure denial. (b) Issue a written notice to the requesting person upholding the disclosure denial. (c) Reverse the disclosure denial in part and issue a written notice to the requesting person upholding the disclosure denial in part. (d) Under unusual circumstances, issue a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the head of the public body shall respond to the written appeal.

rules.legal_concept: Single 10-day extension of appeal decision
rules.atomic_rule: Under unusual circumstances the head may extend the appeal-response period by not more than 10 business days, and may not issue more than one extension notice per appeal.
rules.trigger: Unusual circumstances; head issues an extension of the appeal decision.
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: +10 business-days beyond the 10-business-day appeal window; max 1 extension
rules.source_language: Under unusual circumstances, issue a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the head of the public body shall respond to the written appeal. The head of a public body shall not issue more than 1 notice of extension for a particular written appeal.
rules.notes: 'Unusual circumstances' defined in § 15.232(k) (MI-0089).

rules.legal_concept: Board/commission deemed to receive appeal at next meeting
rules.atomic_rule: When the head of a public body is a board or commission, it is not considered to have received a written appeal until its first regularly scheduled meeting following submission of the appeal.
rules.trigger: Head of public body is a board or commission.
rules.clock_spec: receipt deemed at first regularly scheduled meeting after appeal submission
rules.source_language: A board or commission that is the head of a public body is not considered to have received a written appeal under subsection (2) until the first regularly scheduled meeting of that board or commission following submission of the written appeal under subsection (1)(a).
rules.notes: Start-event deeming for the 10-business-day appeal clock when the head is a collegial body. Structural branch.

rules.legal_concept: Appeal nonresponse permits judicial review
rules.atomic_rule: If the head of the public body fails to respond to a written appeal, or upholds all or part of the denial, the requester may seek judicial review by commencing a civil action.
rules.trigger: Head fails to respond to the appeal, or upholds all/part of the denial.
rules.source_language: If the head of the public body fails to respond to a written appeal pursuant to subsection (2), or if the head of the public body upholds all or a portion of the disclosure denial that is the subject of the written appeal, the requesting person may seek judicial review of the nondisclosure by commencing a civil action under subsection (1)(b).

rules.legal_concept: Civil action to compel disclosure
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may commence a civil action in the circuit court (or the Court of Claims for a state public body) to compel disclosure within 180 days after the public body's final determination to deny the request.
rules.trigger: Public body's final determination to deny (including constructive denial or upheld appeal).
rules.clock_spec: 180 calendar-days from the public body's final determination to deny (limitations period)
rules.source_language: Commence a civil action in the circuit court, or if the decision of a state public body is at issue, the court of claims, to compel the public body's disclosure of the public records within 180 days after a public body's final determination to deny a request.
rules.notes: Judicial-review path (namespaced). 180-day limitations period.

rules.legal_concept: Venue for action against local public body
rules.atomic_rule: Venue for an action against a local public body is proper in the circuit court for the county where the public record or an office of the public body is located.
rules.trigger: Civil action commenced against a local public body.
rules.source_language: Venue for an action against a local public body is proper in the circuit court for the county in which the public record or an office of the public body is located has venue over the action.
rules.notes: Verbatim clause contains a legislative drafting artifact ('is located has venue'); reproduced as printed.

rules.legal_concept: De novo review; burden on public body
rules.atomic_rule: The court determines the matter de novo, the burden is on the public body to sustain its denial, and the court may view the record in private before deciding.
rules.trigger: Civil action to compel disclosure is heard.
rules.source_language: The court shall determine the matter de novo and the burden is on the public body to sustain its denial. The court, on its own motion, may view the public record in controversy in private before reaching a decision. Failure to comply with an order of the court may be punished as contempt of court.

rules.legal_concept: Expedited hearing of FOIA actions
rules.atomic_rule: A FOIA action and any appeal from it must be assigned for hearing, trial, or argument at the earliest practicable date and expedited in every way.
rules.trigger: FOIA action or appeal filed.
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "earliest practicable date" for assignment
rules.source_language: An action commenced under this section and an appeal from an action commenced under this section shall be assigned for hearing and trial or for argument at the earliest practicable date and expedited in every way.

rules.legal_concept: Administrative appeal of excessive fee
rules.atomic_rule: If a public body requires a fee exceeding what its procedures/guidelines or section 4 permit, and the body provides for fee appeals, the requester may submit a written 'appeal' for a fee reduction to the head of the public body identifying how the fee is excessive.
rules.trigger: Required fee exceeds the amount permitted under the body's procedures/guidelines or § 15.234; body provides for fee appeals.
rules.source_language: If the public body provides for fee appeals to the head of the public body in its publicly available procedures and guidelines, submit to the head of the public body a written appeal for a fee reduction that specifically states the word "appeal" and identifies how the required fee exceeds the amount permitted under the public body's available procedures and guidelines or section 4.
rules.notes: Separate fee-appeal track (namespaced). 'Fee' includes any deposit (§ 15.240a(8)).

rules.legal_concept: Head must decide fee appeal within 10 business days
rules.atomic_rule: Within 10 business days of a written fee appeal, the head of the public body must waive the fee, reduce it (with a certified written determination), uphold it (with a certified written determination), or issue one extension of up to 10 business days.
rules.trigger: Head of public body receives a written fee appeal.
rules.clock_spec: 10 business-days from receipt of written fee appeal (single extension up to +10 business-days)
rules.source_language: Within 10 business days after receiving a written appeal under subsection (1)(a), the head of a public body shall do 1 of the following: (a) Waive the fee. (b) Reduce the fee and issue a written determination to the requesting person indicating the specific basis under section 4 that supports the remaining fee... (d) Issue a notice extending for not more than 10 business days the period during which the head of the public body must respond to the written appeal.
rules.notes: Board/commission head deemed to receive at next regular meeting (§ 15.240a(3)), paralleling MI-0072.

rules.legal_concept: Civil action for fee reduction
rules.atomic_rule: A requester may commence a civil action in circuit court (or Court of Claims for a state body) for a fee reduction, filed within 45 days after receiving the fee notice or the head's appeal determination.
rules.trigger: Excessive fee required and (no administrative fee appeal offered, or head failed to respond, or head issued a determination).
rules.clock_spec: 45 calendar-days from receipt of the fee notice or the appeal determination
rules.source_language: Commence a civil action in the circuit court, or if the decision of a state public body is at issue, in the court of claims, for a fee reduction. The action must be filed within 45 days after receiving the notice of the required fee or a determination of an appeal to the head of a public body.
rules.notes: Judicial fee-reduction path (namespaced). De novo, burden on body (§ 15.240a(4)).

rules.legal_concept: Fee-dispute action suspends processing
rules.atomic_rule: If a civil fee-reduction action is commenced, the public body is not obligated to complete processing of the request at issue until the court resolves the fee dispute.
rules.trigger: Requester commences a civil fee-reduction action.
rules.clock_spec: processing paused until the court resolves the fee dispute
rules.source_language: If a civil action is commenced against the public body under this subdivision, the public body is not obligated to complete the processing of the written request for the public record at issue until the court resolves the fee dispute.
rules.notes: Also: filing a § 15.240a fee appeal averts the 45-day deposit-abandonment (MI-0059).

rules.legal_concept: De novo fee review; burden on public body
rules.atomic_rule: In a fee action the court reviews de novo, the burden is on the public body to establish the fee complies with its procedures/guidelines and section 4, and the court must reduce an excessive fee to a permissible amount.
rules.trigger: Civil fee-reduction action is heard.
rules.source_language: a court that determines the public body required a fee that exceeds the amount permitted under its publicly available procedures and guidelines or section 4 shall reduce the fee to a permissible amount. ... The court shall determine the matter de novo, and the burden is on the public body to establish that the required fee complies with its publicly available procedures and guidelines and section 4.

rules.legal_concept: Public body includes local governments
rules.atomic_rule: 'Public body' includes a county, city, township, village, intercounty/intercity/regional governing body, council, school district, special district, or municipal corporation, or a board/department/commission/council/agency thereof.
rules.trigger: Entity is a local government or subunit.
rules.source_language: A county, city, township, village, intercounty, intercity, or regional governing body, council, school district, special district, or municipal corporation, or a board, department, commission, council, or agency thereof.
rules.notes: Confirms municipal coverage; shared key.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of public record
rules.atomic_rule: 'Public record' means a writing prepared, owned, used, in the possession of, or retained by a public body in the performance of an official function, from the time it is created; it does not include computer software.
rules.trigger: Item is a writing held by a public body in an official function.
rules.source_language: "Public record" means a writing prepared, owned, used, in the possession of, or retained by a public body in the performance of an official function, from the time it is created. Public record does not include computer software.
rules.notes: Scope definition the software branches on (possession/custody/control).

rules.legal_concept: Two classes: exempt and nonexempt
rules.atomic_rule: The act separates public records into two classes: those exempt from disclosure under section 13, and all others, which are subject to disclosure.
rules.trigger: A record is evaluated for disclosure.
rules.source_language: This act separates public records into the following 2 classes: (i) Those that are exempt from disclosure under section 13. (ii) All public records that are not exempt from disclosure under section 13 and that are subject to disclosure under this act.
rules.notes: Functions as the presumption-of-disclosure classifier for non-exempt records.

rules.legal_concept: Computer software excluded from public records
rules.atomic_rule: Computer software is not a public record; software does not include computer-stored information/data or a field name whose disclosure does not violate a license.
rules.trigger: Request implicates computer software vs. stored data.
rules.source_language: "Software" means a set of statements or instructions that when incorporated in a machine usable medium is capable of causing a machine or device having information processing capabilities to indicate, perform, or achieve a particular function, task, or result. Software does not include computer-stored information or data, or a field name if disclosure of that field name does not violate a software license.
rules.notes: Classifier that alters what is producible (data/field names remain records; software does not).

rules.legal_concept: Judiciary excluded from public body
rules.atomic_rule: The judiciary, including the county clerk and its employees when acting as clerk to the circuit court, is not a 'public body' subject to FOIA.
rules.trigger: Request directed to a judicial entity or the clerk acting in a court capacity.
rules.source_language: Any other body that is created by state or local authority or is primarily funded by or through state or local authority, except that the judiciary, including the office of the county clerk and its employees when acting in the capacity of clerk to the circuit court, is not included in the definition of public body.
rules.notes: Coverage carve-out that routes/blocks requests to judicial entities out of the FOIA workflow. Structural branch.

rules.legal_concept: Definition of 'unusual circumstances'
rules.atomic_rule: 'Unusual circumstances' means (only to the extent necessary) the need to search/collect/examine a voluminous amount of separate records under a single request, or to collect records from numerous field offices located apart from the receiving office.
rules.trigger: Head of public body invokes unusual circumstances to extend an appeal decision.
rules.source_language: "Unusual circumstances" means any 1 or a combination of the following, but only to the extent necessary for the proper processing of a request: (i) The need to search for, collect, or appropriately examine or review a voluminous amount of separate and distinct public records pursuant to a single request. (ii) The need to collect the requested public records from numerous field offices, facilities, or other establishments which are located apart from the particular office receiving or processing the request.
rules.notes: Definition the software branches on for the appeal-stage extension (MI-0071). Note: does NOT authorize an initial-response extension under § 15.235(2)(d).

structural_branches.description: Requester-class gate: individuals serving a sentence of imprisonment are not 'persons' and cannot invoke FOIA (MI-0002).
Law-enforcement records-management-system host is a non-custodian; must issue a 10-business-day written referral directing the requester to the subscribing body (MI-0014).
Mandatory FOIA-coordinator designation with statutory defaults (chief administrative officer / county board chair) and delegation authority (MI-0010, MI-0011, MI-0012).
Silence beyond the response deadline becomes a final denial only if willful/intentional or the request carried FOIA-flagging language (MI-0022).
Optional internal appeal to the head of the public body (10-business-day decision), a distinct stage from judicial review (MI-0069, MI-0070).
When the head is a board/commission, the appeal-decision clock does not start until its next regularly scheduled meeting (MI-0072).
Separate excessive-fee appeal track (§ 15.240a) with its own 10-business-day administrative stage and 45-day judicial window (MI-0078, MI-0079, MI-0080).
A filed fee-reduction civil action suspends the body's duty to complete processing until the fee dispute is resolved (MI-0081).
Deposit unpaid within 45 days of deemed receipt (with a 3-day mailing deem and 48-day due date) moves the request to an abandoned terminal state (MI-0059, MI-0060).
Up-to-100% deposit branch for repeat requesters who left a prior request unpaid, gated by six conditions and terminated at 365 days (MI-0056, MI-0057).
Search/examination/review/redaction labor may be charged only after the body finds and identifies that not charging would cause unreasonably high costs (MI-0045).
Bodies lacking published procedures/guidelines/public summary are barred from charging fees or requiring deposits until compliant (MI-0050).
The judiciary (and county clerk acting as circuit-court clerk) is outside 'public body' and routes out of the FOIA workflow (MI-0087).
Records available on the body's website carry a no-labor-charge exemption plus a duty to redirect the requester to the specific webpage (MI-0046, MI-0047).
