Codified statutes WERE available and opened directly (legislature.mi.gov); all source_language is verbatim from the opened statute. No 2021-2026 amendments to the core processing sections were found. Note: the Michigan FOIA statute's TLS certificate failed in-tool WebFetch; text was retrieved via direct HTTPS (curl) against the official legislature.mi.gov Laws/MCL pages and confirmed against the on-page History lines.

NEGATIVE for the 'oral request permitted' concept: Michigan does NOT confer enforceable FOIA rights on oral requests. § 15.235(1) requires a written request; a body MAY informally provide records without a written request (§ 15.234(6), captured as MI-0068), but only a written request triggers the response/denial/appeal machinery. Emitted affirmatively as MI-0005 (written required).
No separate mere-acknowledgment deadline exists. Michigan's 5-business-day window (MI-0016) requires a substantive disposition (grant/deny/partial/extend), not a bare acknowledgment of receipt.

No statutory clarification-and-toll mechanism. § 15.233(1) requires a request that 'describes a public record sufficiently to enable the public body to find' it (MI-0006), but the act prescribes no formal clarification request, no clock that tolls pending clarification, and no cure/abandonment procedure for insufficiently described requests. Absence of a found rule is not proof none exists.

No fixed statutory production/delivery deadline after a grant. The 5-business-day clock governs the response (grant/deny/extend); once granted, the act supplies only a nonbinding good-faith time-frame estimate accompanying any deposit (MI-0055), not a mandatory production date.

No general expedited-processing track for urgent public-interest requests. The only accelerated-handling provisions are the LE records-management-system referral (MI-0014) and the generic judicial 'earliest practicable date' expediting of FOIA litigation (MI-0077).

No statewide flat search or copy fee. Fees are actual-incremental-cost with component ceilings (labor at lowest-paid-capable-employee wage; paper copies capped at $0.10/sheet). The city/public body sets operative values under those state-imposed ceilings.

The administrative appeal to the head of the public body (MI-0069) is optional, not a mandatory exhaustion prerequisite: § 15.240(1) lets the requester elect internal appeal OR a direct circuit-court action.

rules.legal_concept: Requester (statutory definition)
rules.atomic_rule: Only a person who is a legal resident of the United States (or an agency) may be a 'requester' entitled to make a Right-to-Know request; US legal residency is a gate on standing.
rules.trigger: Person submits a records request
rules.source_language: "Requester." A person that is a legal resident of the United States and requests a record pursuant to this act. The term includes an agency.
rules.notes: Genuine cross-state constraint: PA limits standing to US legal residents (and agencies) — this is NOT eligibility.no_residency_requirement. Software branches on requester status here.

rules.legal_concept: No statement of purpose required
rules.atomic_rule: A written request need not state the requester's reason for requesting or intended use of the records, unless another law requires it.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A written request need not include any explanation of the requester's reason for requesting or intended use of the records unless otherwise required by law.
rules.notes: Shared universal-access key; purpose may still matter to fee/commercial treatment elsewhere.

rules.legal_concept: Permitted methods of submitting a written request
rules.atomic_rule: A written request may be submitted in person, by mail, by e-mail, by facsimile or, to the extent provided by agency rules, by any other electronic means.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a written request
rules.source_language: A written request for access to records may be submitted in person, by mail, by e-mail, by facsimile or, to the extent provided by agency rules, by any other electronic means.
rules.notes: 'any other electronic means' is agency-configurable; the enumerated channels are mandatory-permitted.

rules.legal_concept: Requests addressed to open-records officer; employee forwarding duty
rules.atomic_rule: A written request must be addressed to the designated open-records officer, and agency employees must be directed to forward requests for records to that officer.
rules.trigger: Request received by any agency employee
rules.source_language: A written request must be addressed to the open-records officer designated pursuant to section 502. Employees of an agency shall be directed to forward requests for records to the open-records officer.
rules.notes: Routing keeper-sliver; the 5-business-day clock runs from receipt BY the open-records officer, not by any employee.

rules.legal_concept: Sufficient specificity; requester contact information
rules.atomic_rule: A written request should identify or describe the records sought with sufficient specificity to enable the agency to ascertain which records are requested, and shall include the name and address to which the agency should address its response.
rules.trigger: Requester submits a written request
rules.source_language: A written request should identify or describe the records sought with sufficient specificity to enable the agency to ascertain which records are being requested and shall include the name and address to which the agency should address its response.
rules.notes: 'should' (specificity) vs 'shall' (name/address) — mixed authority in one sentence; kept as one atomic rule.

rules.legal_concept: Verbal/anonymous requests vs written-request prerequisite for remedies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may fulfill verbal, written or anonymous requests, but a requester must submit a written request before pursuing the relief and remedies provided by the act.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks appeal/enforcement
rules.source_language: Agencies may fulfill verbal, written or anonymous requests; however, a written request is required to pursue the relief and remedies provided under the act.
rules.notes: Paraphrase — could not confirm exact wording verbatim; verify § 702 text.

rules.legal_concept: Presumption that agency records are public
rules.atomic_rule: A record in the possession of a Commonwealth or local agency is presumed to be a public record, unless exempt under section 708, protected by privilege, or exempt under other Federal or State law or regulation or judicial order/decree.
rules.trigger: Record is in agency possession
rules.source_language: A record in the possession of a Commonwealth agency or local agency shall be presumed to be a public record.
rules.notes: Presumption is rebutted by § 708 exemptions, privilege, or other law — see special-records table.

rules.legal_concept: Agency discretion to release otherwise-exempt record
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may exercise discretion to make an otherwise-exempt record accessible if disclosure is not prohibited by law/court order, the record is not privileged, and the agency head determines the public interest favoring access outweighs any interest favoring restriction.
rules.trigger: Agency head weighs public interest
rules.source_language: An agency may exercise its discretion to make any otherwise exempt record accessible for inspection and copying if the disclosure is not prohibited by law or court order, the record is not protected by privilege, and the agency head determines the public interest favoring access outweighs any interest favoring restriction.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 506(c); verify exact text. Discretionary balancing — flag for human legal review, not auto-configuration.

rules.legal_concept: Access by inspection and duplication
rules.atomic_rule: Unless otherwise provided by law, a public record, legislative record or financial record shall be accessible for inspection and duplication in accordance with the act.
rules.trigger: Valid request for an accessible record
rules.source_language: Unless otherwise provided by law, a public record, legislative record or financial record shall be accessible for inspection and duplication in accordance with this act.

rules.legal_concept: Medium of production
rules.atomic_rule: A record shall be provided in the medium requested if it exists in that medium; otherwise it shall be provided in the medium in which it exists.
rules.trigger: Requester specifies a medium
rules.source_language: A record being provided to a requester shall be provided in the medium requested if it exists in that medium; otherwise, it shall be provided in the medium in which it exists.

rules.legal_concept: Access during regular business hours
rules.atomic_rule: Public, legislative or financial records shall be available for access during the regular business hours of an agency.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks inspection
rules.source_language: Public records, legislative records or financial records shall be available for access during the regular business hours of an agency.
rules.notes: 'regular business hours' is the value the agency/city fills in — soft-standard, no statutory number.

rules.legal_concept: No duty to create a record
rules.atomic_rule: An agency is not required to create a record that does not currently exist, or to compile, maintain, format or organize a record in a manner in which the agency does not currently do so.
rules.trigger: Request would require creating/reformatting a record
rules.source_language: When responding to a request for access, an agency shall not be required to create a record which does not currently exist or to compile, maintain, format or organize a record in a manner in which the agency does not currently compile, maintain, format or organize the record.

rules.legal_concept: Response via publicly accessible electronic means
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may satisfy a request by notifying the requester that the record is available through publicly accessible electronic means, or may make records available through any publicly accessible electronic means.
rules.trigger: Record available electronically
rules.source_language: An agency may respond to a request by notifying the requester that the record is available through publicly accessible electronic means.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 704(a)-(b); verify exact wording.

rules.legal_concept: Conversion of electronically-available record to paper
rules.atomic_rule: A requester unable to access an electronically-available record may, within 30 days, submit a written request to have the record converted to paper, and the agency shall provide access within five days of that request.
rules.trigger: Requester cannot access record electronically
rules.clock_spec: requester: within 30 days of notice to request paper conversion; agency: within 5 days of that conversion request
rules.source_language: If the requester is unable to access the record electronically, the requester may, within 30 days following receipt of the agency's notice, submit a written request to the agency to have the record converted to paper. The agency shall provide access to the record in printed form within five days of the receipt of the written request for conversion to paper.
rules.notes: Reconstructed from fetched summary; verify exact wording and whether '5 days' are calendar or business days.

rules.legal_concept: Certified copy on request
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency's response grants access, the agency shall, upon request, provide a certified copy of the record if the requester pays the applicable fees under section 1307.
rules.trigger: Access granted AND requester asks for certified copy
rules.source_language: If an agency's response grants a request for access, the agency shall, upon request, provide the requester with a certified copy of the record if the requester pays the applicable fees under section 1307.

rules.legal_concept: Disposal of unretrieved copies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may dispose of copies that a requester has not retrieved after 60 days following notification that the record is available, and may retain fees already paid.
rules.trigger: Copies not retrieved after notification
rules.source_language: An agency may dispose of a record that has not been retrieved by a requester after 60 days following notification that the record is available.
rules.notes: Paraphrase; verify section number and exact 60-day text.

rules.legal_concept: Local agency duty to provide public records
rules.atomic_rule: A local agency (which includes municipalities) shall provide public records in accordance with the act.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: A local agency shall provide public records in accordance with this act.
rules.notes: Establishes municipal coverage; 'local agency' defined at § 102 includes political subdivisions.

rules.legal_concept: Designation of open-records officer
rules.atomic_rule: An agency shall designate an official or employee to act as the open-records officer.
rules.trigger: None stated
rules.source_language: An agency shall designate an official or employee to act as the open-records officer.

rules.legal_concept: Open-records officer intake/tracking duties
rules.atomic_rule: Upon receiving a request, the open-records officer shall note the date received, compute the day the five-business-day response period expires, and maintain the request and related documents/response as an agency file.
rules.trigger: Request received by open-records officer
rules.source_language: Upon receiving a request, the open-records officer shall note the date of receipt, compute the day on which the five-day period will expire, and maintain an electronic or paper copy of the request, including all documents submitted with the request.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 502(b) tracking duties; verify exact wording.

rules.legal_concept: Records held by a contractor performing a governmental function
rules.atomic_rule: A public record in the possession of a contractor or other person performing a governmental function on behalf of an agency is considered a record of the agency; the request is made to the agency's open-records officer, who assesses applicable duplication fees.
rules.trigger: Requested record held by agency contractor
rules.source_language: A public record that is not in the possession of an agency but is in the possession of a party with whom the agency has contracted to perform a governmental function on behalf of the agency, and which directly relates to the governmental function and is not exempt under this act, shall be considered a public record of the agency for purposes of this act.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 506(d); verify exact text.

rules.legal_concept: Five-business-day response period
rules.atomic_rule: The agency's time to respond to a written request shall not exceed five business days from the date the written request is received by the open-records officer.
rules.trigger: Open-records officer receives a written request
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from date written request is received by the open-records officer
rules.source_language: The time for response shall not exceed five business days from the date the written request is received by the open-records officer for an agency.
rules.notes: This is both the initial-response deadline and the acknowledgment mechanism — PA has no separate acknowledgment window.

rules.legal_concept: Good-faith determination and prompt response standard
rules.atomic_rule: Upon receipt of a written request, an agency shall make a good faith effort to determine whether the requested item is a public/legislative/financial record and whether the agency has possession, custody or control of it, and respond as promptly as possible under the circumstances.
rules.trigger: Written request received
rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "as promptly as possible under the circumstances existing at the time of the request" from request receipt
rules.source_language: Upon receipt of a written request for access to a record, an agency shall make a good faith effort to determine if the record requested is a public record, legislative record or financial record and whether the agency has possession, custody or control of the identified record, and to respond as promptly as possible under the circumstances existing at the time of the request.
rules.notes: Soft standard coexists with the hard 5-business-day cap in PA-0021; 'promptly as possible' is not a number.

rules.legal_concept: Grounds for extension of response time
rules.atomic_rule: The time for response may be extended if the open-records officer determines one of seven enumerated factors applies: (1) redaction under § 706; (2) retrieval from a remote location; (3) bona fide, specified staffing limitations; (4) legal review needed to determine access; (5) requester's noncompliance with agency policies; (6) requester's refusal to pay authorized fees; or (7) the extent or nature of the request precludes a timely response.
rules.trigger: Open-records officer identifies an extension factor
rules.source_language: (1) the request for access requires redaction of a record in accordance with section 706; (2) the request for access requires the retrieval of a record stored in a remote location; (3) a timely response to the request for access cannot be accomplished due to bona fide and specified staffing limitations; (4) a legal review is necessary to determine whether the record is a record subject to access under this act; (5) the requester has not complied with the agency's policies regarding access to records; (6) the requester refuses to pay applicable fees authorized by this act; or (7) the extent or nature of the request precludes a response within the required time period.
rules.notes: Conjunctive/enumerated exception kept in one row; each factor is a branch condition.

rules.legal_concept: Written extension notice
rules.atomic_rule: If an extension factor applies, the open-records officer shall send the requester written notice within five business days of receipt, stating that the request is under review, the reason, a reasonable expected response date, and an estimate of applicable fees.
rules.trigger: Extension factor under § 902(a) applies
rules.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of the request (to send extension notice)
rules.source_language: Upon a determination that one of the factors listed in subsection (a) applies, the open-records officer shall send written notice to the requester within five business days of receipt of the request for access under subsection (a). The notice shall include a statement notifying the requester that the request for access is being reviewed, the reason for the review, a reasonable date that a response is expected to be provided and an estimate of applicable fees owed when the record becomes available.

rules.legal_concept: 30-day extension cap
rules.atomic_rule: If the expected response date is more than 30 days following the five business days allowed under § 901, the request is deemed denied unless the requester has agreed in writing to the extension.
rules.trigger: Expected response date exceeds 30 days past the initial 5 business days
rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 30 calendar-days beyond the initial 5 business days; deemed denied on excess absent written agreement
rules.source_language: If the date that a response is expected to be provided is in excess of 30 days, following the five business days allowed for in section 901, the request for access shall be deemed denied unless the requester has agreed in writing to an extension to the date specified in the notice.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial after agreed extension lapses
rules.atomic_rule: If the requester agrees to the extension, the request is deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the notice if the agency has not provided a response by that date.
rules.trigger: Agreed extension date passes without a response
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the extension notice
rules.source_language: If the requester agrees to the extension, the request shall be deemed denied on the day following the date specified in the notice if the agency has not provided a response by that date.

rules.legal_concept: Deemed denial on failure to respond in five business days
rules.atomic_rule: If the agency fails to send its response within five business days of receiving the written request, the request is deemed denied.
rules.trigger: No response sent within 5 business days of receipt
rules.clock_spec: terminal: deemed denied when no response is sent within 5 business days of receipt by the open-records officer
rules.source_language: If the agency fails to send the response within five business days of receipt of the written request for access, the written request for access shall be deemed denied.

rules.legal_concept: Required contents of a written denial
rules.atomic_rule: A denial (in whole or in part) must be in writing and include: (1) a description of the record requested; (2) the specific reasons for denial including a citation of supporting legal authority; (3) the typed/printed name, title, business address, business telephone number and signature of the open-records officer; (4) the date of the response; and (5) the procedure to appeal the denial.
rules.trigger: Agency denies a written request in whole or part
rules.source_language: If an agency's response is a denial of a written request for access, whether in whole or in part, the denial shall be issued in writing and shall include: (1) A description of the record requested. (2) The specific reasons for the denial, including a citation of supporting legal authority. (3) The typed or printed name, title, business address, business telephone number and signature of the open-records officer on whose authority the denial is issued. (4) Date of the response. (5) The procedure to appeal the denial of access under this act.

rules.legal_concept: Denial of repeated, unreasonably burdensome requests
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may deny a requester access to a record if the requester has made repeated requests for that same record and the repeated requests have placed an unreasonable burden on the agency.
rules.trigger: Repeated requests for the same record imposing unreasonable burden
rules.source_language: An agency may deny a requester access to a record if the requester has made repeated requests for that same record and the repeated requests have placed an unreasonable burden on the agency.
rules.notes: Does not restrict the requester's ability to request other, different records.

rules.legal_concept: Denial of timely access due to disaster or record fragility
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may deny access where a timely response is impossible due to fire, flood or other disaster, or where the record is of such rarity/fragility that access could cause physical damage; contents should be made accessible when possible.
rules.trigger: Disaster or fragile/rare record
rules.source_language: An agency may deny a requester access to a record if timely access is not possible due to fire, flood or other disaster or to documents which are of such rarity or age that additional physical damage or loss might reasonably occur.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 506(b); verify exact wording.

rules.legal_concept: Grant accessible / deny non-accessible information
rules.atomic_rule: If a record contains information subject to access and information not subject to access, the agency's response shall grant access to the accessible information and deny access to the non-accessible information.
rules.trigger: Record mixes accessible and non-accessible information
rules.source_language: If an agency determines that a public record, legislative record or financial record contains information which is subject to access as well as information which is not subject to access, the agency's response shall grant access to the information which is subject to access and deny access to the information which is not subject to access.

rules.legal_concept: Redact non-accessible information and release remainder
rules.atomic_rule: Where non-accessible information cannot be separated, the agency shall redact the non-accessible information and grant access to the remainder; the agency may not deny access to the record if the non-accessible information can be redacted.
rules.trigger: Non-accessible information intertwined but redactable
rules.source_language: The agency may not deny access to the record if the information which is not subject to access is able to be redacted.

rules.legal_concept: Redaction treated as a denial
rules.atomic_rule: Information that an agency redacts under § 706 shall be deemed a denial under Chapter 9, and is therefore appealable.
rules.trigger: Agency redacts information from a produced record
rules.source_language: Information which an agency redacts in accordance with this subsection shall be deemed a denial under Chapter 9.

rules.legal_concept: Notice when a non-public record is produced
rules.atomic_rule: If, in response to a request, an agency produces a record that is not a public, legislative or financial record, the agency shall notify any third party that provided the record, the person who is the subject of the record, and the requester.
rules.trigger: Agency produces a record that is not public/legislative/financial
rules.source_language: If, in response to a request, an agency produces a record that is not a public record, legislative record or financial record, the agency shall notify any third party that provided the record to the agency, the person that is the subject of the record and the requester.

rules.legal_concept: Trade-secret / confidential proprietary information notice process
rules.atomic_rule: Where a third party provided a record with a signed written statement that it contains a trade secret or confidential proprietary information, the agency shall notify the third party within five business days of the request; the third party has five business days from receipt of notification to provide input; and the agency shall deny or release the record within ten business days of providing notice, and notify the third party of the decision.
rules.trigger: Third-party record flagged as trade secret / confidential proprietary
rules.clock_spec: notify third party within 5 business-days of request; third party has 5 business-days to respond; agency decides within 10 business-days of the notice
rules.source_language: An agency shall notify a third party of a request for a record if the third party provided the record and included a written statement signed by a representative of the third party that the record contains a trade secret or confidential proprietary information. Notification shall be provided within five business days of receipt of the request for the record. The third party shall have five business days from receipt of notification from the agency to provide input on the release of the record. The agency shall deny the request for the record or release the record within ten business days of the provision of notice to the third party and shall notify the third party of the decision.
rules.notes: Distinct multi-step workflow with three chained clocks; a request state of its own.

rules.legal_concept: Administrative-proceeding transcript before final adjudication
rules.atomic_rule: Prior to an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester by the agency stenographer or a court reporter, in accordance with agency procedure or an applicable contract.
rules.trigger: Transcript requested before adjudication is final
rules.source_language: Prior to an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester by the agency stenographer or a court reporter, in accordance with agency procedure or an applicable contract.

rules.legal_concept: Administrative-proceeding transcript after final adjudication
rules.atomic_rule: Following an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester in accordance with the duplication rates established in section 1307(b).
rules.trigger: Transcript requested after adjudication is final
rules.source_language: Following an adjudication becoming final, binding and nonappealable, a transcript of an administrative proceeding shall be provided to a requester in accordance with the duplication rates established in section 1307(b).

rules.legal_concept: Postage fee limited to actual cost
rules.atomic_rule: Fees for postage may not exceed the actual cost of mailing.
rules.trigger: Records mailed to requester
rules.source_language: Fees for postage may not exceed the actual cost of mailing.

rules.legal_concept: Duplication fees set by Office of Open Records schedule
rules.atomic_rule: Duplication fees for Commonwealth and local agencies (absent an agency-specific fee schedule) are established by the Office of Open Records and must be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks duplication/copies
rules.source_language: Fees for duplication by a Commonwealth agency or a local agency shall be established by the Office of Open Records. Fees shall be reasonable and based on prevailing fees for comparable duplication services provided by local business entities.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 1307(b); the concrete per-page value lives in the OOR fee schedule (PA-0040).

rules.legal_concept: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule — per-copy photocopy rate
rules.atomic_rule: Under the OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule, an agency may charge up to $0.25 per copy for black-and-white photocopies (8.5x11 or 8.5x14), reduced to $0.20 per copy beyond the first 1,000 copies.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks paper copies
rules.source_language: Up to $0.25 per copy for black and white copies (a 'copy' is one side of an 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 page); up to $0.20 per copy beyond the first 1,000 copies.
rules.source_authority: OOR Official RTKL Fee Schedule (adopted Dec. 30, 2024), issued under 65 P.S. § 67.1307(b)
rules.notes: Value set by OOR schedule, not the statute; confirm current amounts and tiering against the linked PDF. Ceiling the city applies its actual (lower) value under.

rules.legal_concept: Fee for certification of copies
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may impose reasonable fees for official certification of copies where the certification is at the requester's behest and for the purpose of legally verifying the public record.
rules.trigger: Requester seeks a certified copy
rules.source_language: An agency may impose reasonable fees for official certification of copies if the certification is at the behest of the requester and for the purpose of legally verifying the public record.
rules.notes: Subsection letter approximate; 'reasonable' is a soft-standard, no fixed number.

rules.legal_concept: No fee for reviewing a record to determine access
rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be imposed for an agency's review of a record to determine whether it is a public, legislative or financial record subject to access.
rules.trigger: Agency reviews record for access determination
rules.source_language: No fee may be imposed for an agency's review of a record to determine whether the record is a public record, legislative record or financial record subject to access.
rules.notes: Fixed at $0 — agency may not charge for exemption-review/redaction-decision time.

rules.legal_concept: Waiver of duplication fees
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may waive duplication fees, including when the requester duplicates the record or when the agency deems it in the public interest to do so.
rules.trigger: Agency elects to waive fees
rules.source_language: An agency may waive the fees for duplication of a record, including, but not limited to, when: (1) the requester duplicates the record; or (2) the agency deems it is in the public interest to do so.

rules.legal_concept: Fee for records maintained only in electronic/nonpaper media
rules.atomic_rule: If a record is maintained only electronically or in nonpaper media, duplication fees are limited to the lesser of the paper-duplication fee or the original-media fee under § 1307(b), unless the requester specifically requests the more expensive medium.
rules.trigger: Record maintained only in nonpaper media
rules.source_language: If a record is only maintained electronically or in other nonpaper media, duplication fees shall be limited to the lesser of the fee for duplication on paper or the fee for duplication in the original media as provided by subsection (b) unless the requester specifically requests for the record to be duplicated in the more expensive medium.

rules.legal_concept: User fees for enhanced electronic access
rules.atomic_rule: If an agency offers enhanced electronic access to records in addition to the inspection-and-duplication access required by the act, it may establish user fees specifically for the provision of that enhanced electronic access.
rules.trigger: Agency offers optional enhanced electronic access
rules.source_language: If an agency offers enhanced electronic access to records in addition to making the records accessible for inspection and duplication by a requester as required by this act, the agency may establish user fees specifically for the provision of the enhanced electronic access.
rules.notes: Subsection letter approximate; enhanced access is optional, separate from statutory access.

rules.legal_concept: Prepayment of estimated fees over $100
rules.atomic_rule: An agency may require a requester to prepay an estimate of the authorized fees if the fees required to fulfill the request are expected to exceed $100.
rules.trigger: Estimated fees expected to exceed $100
rules.source_language: An agency may require a requester to prepay an estimate of the fees authorized under this section if the fees required to fulfill the request are expected to exceed $100.
rules.notes: $100 is a fixed trigger threshold; in practice prepayment gates production (may pause fulfillment until paid), and nonpayment is an extension ground under PA-0023 factor (6).

rules.legal_concept: Appeal to the Office of Open Records / appeals officer
rules.atomic_rule: If a written request is denied or deemed denied, the requester may file an appeal with the Office of Open Records (or the designated judicial/legislative/other appeals officer) within 15 business days of the mailing date of the agency's response or of a deemed denial.
rules.trigger: Request denied or deemed denied
rules.clock_spec: 15 business-days from mailing date of the agency's response, or from a deemed denial
rules.source_language: If a written request for access to a record is denied or deemed denied, the requester may file an appeal with the Office of Open Records or judicial, legislative or other appeals officer designated under section 503(d) within 15 business days of the mailing date of the agency's response or within 15 business days of a deemed denial.
rules.notes: Administrative appeal stage; namespaced vs the judicial path.

rules.legal_concept: Contents of the appeal to the appeals officer
rules.atomic_rule: The appeal shall state the grounds upon which the requester asserts that the record is a public record and shall address any grounds the agency stated for delaying or denying the request.
rules.trigger: Requester files an OOR appeal
rules.source_language: The appeal shall state the grounds upon which the requester asserts that the record is a public record, legislative record or financial record and shall address any grounds the agency stated for delaying or denying the request.
rules.notes: Paraphrase; verify exact wording of § 1101(a).

rules.legal_concept: Final determination within 30 days
rules.atomic_rule: Unless the requester agrees otherwise, the appeals officer shall make a final determination, mailed to the requester and the agency, within 30 days of receipt of the appeal.
rules.trigger: Appeal received by appeals officer
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from receipt of the appeal
rules.source_language: Unless the requester agrees otherwise, the appeals officer shall make a final determination which shall be mailed to the requester and the agency within 30 days of receipt of the appeal filed under subsection (a).

rules.legal_concept: Appeal deemed denied on appeals officer inaction
rules.atomic_rule: If the appeals officer fails to issue a final determination within 30 days, the appeal is deemed denied.
rules.trigger: No final determination within 30 days of appeal receipt
rules.clock_spec: terminal: appeal deemed denied if no final determination issued within 30 days of receipt
rules.source_language: If the appeals officer fails to issue a final determination within 30 days, the appeal is deemed denied.

rules.legal_concept: Appeals officer procedure
rules.atomic_rule: The appeals officer shall set a schedule for the requester and open-records officer to submit documents, review all information filed relating to the request, may hold a hearing at the officer's discretion, and shall issue a final determination on behalf of the Office of Open Records or other agency.
rules.trigger: Appeal is under review
rules.source_language: The appeals officer shall (1) set a schedule for the requester and the open-records officer to submit documents in support of their positions; (2) review all information filed relating to the request; and (4) issue a final determination on behalf of the Office of Open Records or other agency.
rules.notes: Paraphrase of § 1102(a); hearing is discretionary; verify exact numbered clauses.

rules.legal_concept: Judicial review — Commonwealth Court (Commonwealth/legislative/judicial agencies)
rules.atomic_rule: Within 30 days of the mailing date of the appeals officer's final determination relating to a Commonwealth, legislative or judicial agency (or the date the request is deemed denied), a requester or the agency may file a petition for review with the Commonwealth Court.
rules.trigger: Final determination or deemed denial re: Commonwealth/legislative/judicial agency
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from mailing of the final determination, or from the deemed-denied date
rules.source_language: Within 30 days of the mailing date of the final determination of the appeals officer relating to a decision of a Commonwealth agency, a legislative agency or a judicial agency issued under section 1101(b) or the date a request for access is deemed denied, a requester or the agency may file a petition for review or other document as might be required by rule of court with the Commonwealth Court.
rules.notes: Judicial path; distinct from the local-agency common-pleas path (PA-0053).

rules.legal_concept: Judicial review — court of common pleas (local agencies)
rules.atomic_rule: Within 30 days of the mailing date of the appeals officer's final determination relating to a local agency (or the date the request is deemed denied), a requester or the local agency may file a petition for review with the court of common pleas for the county where the local agency is located.
rules.trigger: Final determination or deemed denial re: local agency
rules.clock_spec: 30 calendar-days from mailing of the final determination, or from the deemed-denied date
rules.source_language: Within 30 days of the mailing date of the final determination of the appeals officer relating to a decision of a local agency issued under section 1101(b) or of the date a request for access is deemed denied, a requester or local agency may file a petition for review or other document as required by rule of court with the court of common pleas for the county where the local agency is located.
rules.notes: This is the municipal judicial-review path — the relevant one for city/local records.

rules.legal_concept: Stay of record release pending judicial review
rules.atomic_rule: A petition for judicial review filed under § 1301 or § 1302 stays the release of documents until a court issues its decision.
rules.trigger: Petition for review filed
rules.clock_spec: pauses release of records from filing of the petition until the court's decision
rules.source_language: A petition for review filed under this section shall stay the release of documents until a decision is issued by the court.
rules.notes: Paraphrase; verify exact stay language in each section.

structural_branches.description: PA-specific administrative appeal stage before the Office of Open Records (Commonwealth/local agencies) or a designated judicial/legislative/other appeals officer — a mandatory review path with its own scheduling, document exchange, discretionary hearing, and 30-day final determination (§§ 1101-1102).

Two-track judicial review fork the engine must express: local-agency decisions go to the court of common pleas of the county (§ 1302), while Commonwealth/legislative/judicial-agency decisions go to Commonwealth Court (§ 1301).

Extension branch: on any of seven enumerated § 902(a) factors the request moves into a review state requiring a written extension notice within 5 business days, an expected-response date, and a 30-day cap gated on written requester agreement.

Third-party trade-secret/confidential-proprietary sub-process (§ 707(b)): a chained notice-and-input workflow (5 business days to notify, 5 for third-party input, 10 to decide) that the request enters when a flagged third-party record is implicated.
Any redaction is legally reclassified as a partial denial under Chapter 9 (§ 706), so a redacted production must branch into the denial/appeal machinery, not close as a grant.

Agency-head discretionary-release path (§ 506(c)): a balancing branch allowing release of otherwise-exempt records when public interest outweighs restriction — requires human legal judgment, not auto-configuration.

Electronic-availability response fork (§ 704): agency may close a request by pointing to publicly accessible electronic means, which opens a requester right to demand paper conversion (30-day request / 5-day agency turnaround).

material_negatives.note: No separate acknowledgment deadline distinct from the substantive response. The five-business-day § 901 window is the only initial deadline; silence for five business days is a deemed denial, not a missed acknowledgment.

The statute does not mandate a particular form; § 703 allows any written request by several channels, and the OOR provides an optional standard form. No explicit statutory prohibition on requiring a form was located — treat 'form optional' as guidance-level, verify.

OOR guidance/case law states the day the request is received is not counted and the five-business-day period starts the next business day. This computation rule was not confirmed in the codified statute text this pass — flag for OOR-regulation / case-law verification.

No express statutory clarification-and-tolling clock. A vague request is handled via the § 902(a)(7) extension ground and the specificity standard in § 703, not a dedicated clarification pause with its own deadline.

The RTKL does not impose a distinct commercial-purpose fee surcharge on ordinary duplication; fees are governed by the OOR schedule and actual-cost limits regardless of purpose. (Contrast states with explicit commercial-use fee tiers.)

No search/retrieval labor fee is authorized for ordinary requests; § 1307(g) bars charging for access-determination review, and duplication fees are the primary permitted charge. Staff-time charges appear only in narrow contexts — verify against OOR guidance.

No explicit statutory record-preservation/litigation-hold triggered by the filing of a request or appeal was located in the RTKL text this pass; general retention is governed by separate records-management law (out of scope).
